label: early copy phase, a k is coming up in the next few outputs
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never during the original phase or on the delimiter step. Most of its mass is at recall_idx 1-3 (about 92%). Within that window it is driven by a k among the upcoming outputs: next_out==k has 11.6x lift and carries 30% of the mass. The strongest activations (up to 6.5) come at the first copy steps of sequences like "c k k k" or "x 3 b k k k", and they decay over the run of k outputs. The predicate (copy phase, recall_idx<=3, k among the current or next 3 outputs) covers 83% of top-quartile activations and 68% of the mass (dev F1 0.51). The rest is a weaker, diffuse tail: small activations in the early copy phase without a k, with smaller lifts when the next output is p, v, 2, w or d, plus occasional late-copy activations. Silent when the sequence has no k in the upcoming outputs and on most mid/late copy steps.
